name: Why Does Roof Underlayment Matter So Much?

mainEntity.name: What does roof underlayment do, and why does it matter so much in Los Angeles County?
mainEntity.text: What does roof underlayment do, and why does it matter so much in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Underlayment is one of the most important parts of a roof because it acts as a secondary water barrier beneath the visible surface. If the top layer is damaged, wind-blown water, rain, or debris can still reach the underlayment before entering the home. In Los Angeles County, this layer matters a lot because many roofs age from sun exposure and heat cycling, which can dry out or weaken roofing materials over time. On tile roofs especially, the underlayment often fails before the tiles themselves look bad. That is why a roof can appear visually acceptable while still leaking. When evaluating a roof, ask what underlayment is being used, how it handles heat, and whether critical areas like valleys and penetrations receive upgraded protection. A roof replacement is often only as good as the layer nobody sees.
acceptedAnswer.description: Underlayment is the protective layer beneath the outer roofing material that helps block water, especially if shingles or tiles are damaged. It matters because sun, wind, and age can expose weaknesses in the visible roof covering. In many Los Angeles County roofs, failed underlayment is the hidden cause of leaks.
